body_html:
Good morning messages in Spanish are one of the simplest ways to show someone you care, whether it is your partner, your mom in Guadalajara or a group chat of friends. In many Spanish-speaking families, a morning text, often with a picture or a blessing, is a daily ritual. Below are forty good morning messages to copy and send, grouped by who you are writing to, with English translations and notes on tone.

Quick answer
  • Basic: ¡Buenos días! Casual: ¡Buen día!
  • Sweet: Buenos días, mi amor. Que tengas un día precioso.
  • For family: Buenos días, mamá. Que Dios te bendiga.
  • Use ¡Buen día! in Argentina and Uruguay; ¡Buenos días! everywhere.
{{toc}}

Short good morning messages in Spanish

  1. ¡Buenos días!
    Good morning!
  2. ¡Buen día!
    Good morning! (casual, very common in Argentina)
  3. ¡Buenos días! ¿Cómo amaneciste?
    Good morning! How did you sleep? (literally: how did you wake up?)
  4. Que tengas un lindo día.
    Have a lovely day.
  5. ¡Arriba, que hoy es un gran día!
    Up you get, today is a great day!
  6. Café y buena actitud. ¡Buenos días!
    Coffee and a good attitude. Good morning!
  7. Feliz lunes, ¡a darle con todo!
    Happy Monday, let’s go for it!

¿Cómo amaneciste? is especially natural in Mexico and Colombia. It asks how you woke up, and the usual answer is Bien, gracias, ¿y tú?

For your partner

  1. Buenos días, mi amor. Ya te extraño.
    Good morning, my love. I miss you already.
  2. Despertar pensando en ti es lo mejor de mi día.
    Waking up thinking about you is the best part of my day.
  3. Buenos días, guapa. Que tu día sea tan bonito como tú.
    Good morning, beautiful. May your day be as lovely as you.
  4. Buenos días, guapo. Te mando un beso y un abrazo enorme.
    Good morning, handsome. Sending you a kiss and a big hug.
  5. No hay mejor manera de empezar el día que diciéndote que te quiero.
    There’s no better way to start the day than telling you I love you.
  6. Ojalá estuvieras aquí para tomar el café juntos.
    I wish you were here to have coffee together.
  7. Buenos días, corazón. Hoy va a ser un buen día, ya lo verás.
    Good morning, sweetheart. Today is going to be a good day, you’ll see.
  8. Mi primer pensamiento del día siempre eres tú.
    My first thought of the day is always you.

For more pet names like corazón and mi vida, see {{link:spanish-terms-of-endearment|Spanish terms of endearment}}. If you are far apart, {{link:long-distance-relationship-spanish|long-distance relationship in Spanish}} has messages for time zones.

{{image:2}}

For family

  1. Buenos días, mamá. Que Dios te bendiga hoy y siempre.
    Good morning, Mom. May God bless you today and always.
  2. Buenos días, papá. Que tengas un excelente día en el trabajo.
    Good morning, Dad. Have a great day at work.
  3. Buenos días, familia. Les mando un abrazo a todos.
    Good morning, family. Sending everyone a hug.
  4. Buenos días, abuelita. ¿Cómo amaneció?
    Good morning, Grandma. How did you sleep? (formal)
  5. Que tengan un día lleno de bendiciones.
    Have a day full of blessings. (to several people)
  6. Buenos días, mi niño. ¡Mucho éxito en tu examen!
    Good morning, my boy. Good luck on your exam!

Messages with bendiciones (blessings) are extremely common in family group chats across Latin America, often sent with a flower or sunrise image. Answering with Amén, igualmente (Amen, same to you) is a warm reply.

For friends and coworkers

  1. ¡Buenos días, equipo! A darle.
    Good morning, team! Let’s get to it.
  2. Buenos días. ¿Ya llegó el café o sigo dormido?
    Good morning. Has the coffee arrived or am I still asleep?
  3. ¡Buen día a todos! Que sea un día productivo.
    Good morning, everyone! Have a productive day.
  4. Buenos días, ¿cómo va todo?
    Good morning, how’s everything going?
  5. ¡Feliz viernes! Ya casi es fin de semana.
    Happy Friday! It’s almost the weekend.
  6. Buenos días, amiga. ¡Hoy te va a ir increíble!
    Good morning, my friend. Today is going to go amazingly for you!

For workplace tone, see {{link:talking-to-coworkers-in-spanish|talking to coworkers in Spanish}}.

{{book:love-slowly}}

Funny good morning messages

  1. Buenos días. Mi cama y yo terminamos, pero fue difícil.
    Good morning. My bed and I broke up, but it was hard.
  2. Hoy me levanté con todas las ganas… de seguir durmiendo.
    Today I woke up full of energy… to keep sleeping.
  3. Buenos días a todos menos a la alarma.
    Good morning to everyone except the alarm clock.
  4. Café primero, persona después.
    Coffee first, human later.
  5. Si hoy no puedes con todo, recuerda que mañana tampoco. ¡Buenos días!
    If you can’t handle everything today, remember you won’t tomorrow either. Good morning!

Inspirational good morning messages

  1. Cada mañana es una nueva oportunidad.
    Every morning is a new opportunity.
  2. Sonríe, que hoy puede ser un gran día.
    Smile, today could be a great day.
  3. Poco a poco se va lejos. ¡Buenos días!
    Little by little you go far. Good morning!
  4. Hoy es un buen día para empezar de nuevo.
    Today is a good day to start over.

The third one is a classic proverb; for more, see {{link:spanish-proverbs|Spanish proverbs}}.

{{image:3}}

Tips and common mistakes

  • Buen día vs buenos días. Both are correct. Buen día is typical in Argentina and Uruguay and also common in casual texts elsewhere; buenos días works everywhere.
  • Buenos mañanas. Never correct. “Good morning” is always buenos días.
  • ¿Cómo dormiste? vs ¿cómo amaneciste? Both work. The second sounds warmer in Mexico and Colombia.
  • Formality. With older relatives, use usted: ¿Cómo amaneció? See {{link:tu-vs-usted|tú vs usted}}.

At night, switch to {{link:good-night-messages-in-spanish|good night messages in Spanish}}. The Diccionario panhispánico de dudas confirms that both buen día and buenos días are standard.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

A good morning message in Spanish takes ten seconds to send and can make someone’s day. Pick a few favorites for your partner, family and friends, and make them part of your routine. For more ready-to-send messages, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you say good morning in Spanish?
faq.a: Buenos días, or more casually buen día.

faq.q: How do you say good morning, my love, in Spanish?
faq.a: Buenos días, mi amor. You can also say buenos días, corazón or buenos días, mi vida.
It means “how did you wake up?” or “how did you sleep?”, a warm morning question.
Yes. It is standard and especially common in Argentina and Uruguay.
